title: How Apartheid Worked
summary: Josh and Chuck explain how apartheid in South Africa developed, from Dutch and British colonization in the 1600s through the Afrikaner Nationalist Party's formal apartheid policy starting in 1948 and 1950, the Sharpeville and Soweto massacres, the death of Steve Biko, international sanctions and divestment, and the transition led by F. W. de Klerk and Nelson Mandela in the early 1990s. The episode opens with discussion of the Sun City boycott and blacklist, including Tim Reid's trip, and closes with a listener mail segment about surfing and recommendations of films and music.

segments.title: Opening banter and Sun City blacklist
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with the meaning of the word apartheid in Afrikaans and discuss the 1985 anti-apartheid song Sun Ain't Gonna Play Sun City, the Sun City resort, and the anti-apartheid blacklist of performers who played there, including Tim Reid's publicity trip to South Africa.

segments.title: Dutch and British colonization
segments.summary: The hosts describe how Dutch East India Company settlers arrived in the 1600s as a supply stop on the spice route, then began colonizing, taking indigenous land and using African labor. Britain gained control in the early 1800s and codified master-servant relations.

segments.title: Diamonds, mining and the South Africa Act of 1910
segments.summary: After diamonds and gold were discovered in the 1860s, mining brought harsher segregation and passbooks. The Afrikaner-led government obtained the South Africa Act of 1910, making South Africa a self-governing state with an all-white government.

segments.title: Native Lands Act and early segregation
segments.summary: The Native Lands Act of 1913 confined black South Africans to small, poor parcels of land, starting the segregation period. Black people lost voting rights, union rights and job protections in the following decades.

segments.title: Formal apartheid laws
segments.summary: Apartheid was officially instituted after the Afrikaner Nationalist Party took power, starting with the Population Registration Act of 1950 under D. F. Malan, which classified people as white, Bantu, colored or Indian. Further laws included the Group Areas Act, a ban on interracial marriage, and the Bantu Homelands Act, and Bantu Education Act.

segments.title: Resistance, censorship and Sharpeville
segments.summary: Resistance grew in the 1950s and 1960s. The government tightly controlled news and music, including Rodriguez's record. Police opened fire on peaceful protesters at Sharpeville in 1960, killing 69, after which the ANC and PAC were banned and Mandela went underground and later to prison.

segments.title: Soweto uprising and Steve Biko
segments.summary: Students protesting Afrikaans as the language of instruction in Soweto were shot by police in 1976, and a wave of riots followed with many deaths. Steve Biko, leader of the Black Consciousness movement, was arrested and died in police custody, a death that drew worldwide outrage.

segments.title: International sanctions and divestment
segments.summary: Global pressure grew, with embassies withdrawn and economic sanctions. US Congress passed the Comprehensive Anti-Apartheid Act in 1986 over Reagan's veto. Universities divested from companies doing business in South Africa, with California reportedly divesting about three billion dollars.

segments.title: End of apartheid and transition
segments.summary: In 1989 F. W. de Klerk became president and dismantled apartheid laws through 1993, releasing Mandela. Mandela won the first democratic election, and the two shared the Nobel Peace Prize. The Truth and Reconciliation Commission was set up to hear victims' accounts. The hosts close the topic with film and music recommendations.

segments.title: Listener mail: surfing
segments.summary: Listener Miles, a surf instructor, writes that the surfing episode was accurate and comments on learning to surf, longboards versus shortboards, and invites listeners to contact him. The hosts read out contact information for the show.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Closing reminders for listeners to share expertise and contact the show via social media, email, and the website.
